source.title: Bidirectionally self-normalizing neural networks
source.authors: Yao Lu; S. Gould; Thalaiyasingam Ajanthan

record.file_problem: none; full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests whether its activation normalization and weight constraints affect gradient stability and training accuracy in very deep networks, using a different setup from the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training accuracy after fixed training runs, gradient-norm results, and training-accuracy curves. It does not test random labels, CIFAR-100, residual shortcuts, or the listed above-stability learning-rate behavior. Synthetic-data results involve no training. Cited results from other work are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study compares training accuracy with and without batch normalization in 200-layer fully connected networks, extending V6 to a new setting. It does not isolate initialization effects: GPN changes the activation function, and row-normalized weights are constrained throughout training.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors claim high-probability forward/backward norm preservation under their width, random-orthogonality and activation assumptions, and improved trainability without BN. The real-data experiments use row-normalized weights as a relaxation of orthogonality; the theory is restricted to equal-width fully connected networks.
record.recipe_differences: Uses orthogonal matrices theoretically and row-normalized weights as a practical relaxation, with GPN-transformed activations; experiments are width-500, depth-200 fully connected networks rather than the cited claim recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Activation function and its GPN transformation; batch normalization; dataset (MNIST versus CIFAR-10); width in synthetic gradient-norm experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: GPN activation transformations improve no-BN training accuracy across the tested activations under row-normalized weight constraints; for example, CIFAR-10 ELU improves from 80.73 to 99.37.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation normalization combined with weight constraints maintained throughout training can improve trainability of very deep fully connected networks.

fits_no_version.finding: The theory and synthetic experiments concern forward/backward norm preservation and retained nonlinearity; synthetic experiments perform no training. Real-data gradient-ratio plots show BN-related instability and more stable gradients with GPN without BN.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: GPN activations with orthogonal random weights preserve signal norms under the stated assumptions; related constrained training recipes can stabilize gradients.

record.problems: Real-world experiments cover only MNIST and CIFAR-10 and use fully connected networks. The paper says row-normalized weights are a relaxation of orthogonality. The reported training-accuracy table gives fixed-run endpoints; no uncertainty estimates are reported for those results. The synthetic experiments do not involve training.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying training-accuracy table rows were left out; the test-accuracy values in Table 2 were omitted because the claim concerns training classification error. Gradient-norm plots and training-accuracy curves were not separately extracted as rows because the plotted results are figure-only and the table already reports endpoint training accuracy; the text's explicit gradient-stability conclusions are captured in page excerpts.

untested.parts: Convolutional-network training error, CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, and model-size or regularization effects are not tested. These experiments use fully connected networks.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student optimization or extra-student-neuron comparison.
No depth sweep or matched plain-versus-residual convolutional-network comparison.

No controlled initialization comparison, orthogonal-versus-Gaussian comparison, or trainable-depth sweep. GPN activations and weight constraints maintained during training do not isolate initialization's effect on learning speed or depth.
No learning-rate stability threshold, catapult recovery, or edge-of-stability experiment.

Higher learning-rate tolerance, the original sigmoid/VGG/Inception settings, and Fixup residual networks are untested. Table 2 measures fixed-epoch training accuracy, not time to a matched training-accuracy target; the accuracy trajectories shown in the figures are test accuracy.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for any version. All no-BN rows are retained as V6 comparators; their cannot_determine state means standalone accuracy does not establish BN's effect. BN states use matched activation-and-dataset comparisons. Fixed-epoch endpoints bear on optimization progress but do not establish wall-clock acceleration. No uncertainty is reported for Table 2. Figure-only gradient results and accuracy curves were explicitly declared in rows_left_out, so they are not missing rows.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10 is included, but the study does not test sufficiently large convolutional networks, random or corrupted labels, SGD or Adam from random initialization as stated, or the effects of model size, early stopping, and regularization.
No two-layer teacher-student ReLU experiments or sweep over student and teacher widths.
No depth comparison of plain and residual convolutional networks; the real-world experiments use fully connected networks.

Tests GPN-transformed versus unnormalized activations in deep fully connected networks and reports training accuracy and gradient stability. It does not compare the initialization methods named in the version, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, or trainable depth across depths; the real-world weights are row-normalized as a relaxation of orthogonality.
No sweep over learning rates relative to a stability threshold, curvature tracking, or sharpness measurements.

Reports batch-normalization comparisons in fully connected MNIST and CIFAR-10 experiments, including training accuracy and gradient-norm behavior. It does not test higher learning-rate tolerance, the listed sigmoid/VGG/Inception settings, or Fixup residual networks.
